answer.rationale: A release went out 2 hours ago coinciding with p99 latency climbing 5x. Memory_b1 shows rollback successfully cleared a checkout error spike with prior stable build and no customer impact. Memory_b6 shows staged release gating canary cohorts caught regressions within an hour - supporting that recent releases are a plausible regression source. Settlement traffic at peak means we must preserve writes; a guarded rollback of the suspect build is lower-risk than regional failover (which would lose write locality during peak) and faster than add_capacity (too slow for 90-min degradation). Rollback targets the most likely cause with smallest blast radius and preserves sustained write availability.
